mass_production.ref: Ancient China independently casts standardized hollow-handle bronze spade money (kongshoubu) in the Central Plains
mass_production.ref_zh: 中国中原地区独立铸造空首布等青铜铲币，确立青铜金属铸币传统

sources.title: A History of the World in 100 Objects: Early Lydian Coin — British Museum

notes: 作为国家信用与标准重量保证的金属铸币起源于多中心演化：公元前七至六世纪，小亚细亚吕底亚首创官印冲压琥珀金币，奠定西方打制金银币传统；同期中国中原由贝币演化出空首布等浇铸青铜币，开创东方方孔钱体系。两者工艺与源流独立，具体起源时序与首创权在学界历来并称并存。
notes_en: State-backed metal coinage of standardized weight developed in multiple centers. In the 7th–6th centuries BCE, Lydia in Asia Minor pioneered officially stamped electrum coins, establishing the Western tradition of struck gold and silver coinage. At the same time, China’s Central Plains developed cast-bronze coins such as hollow-handled spade money from shell currency, beginning the East Asian tradition of square-holed coins. Their techniques and origins were independent; scholarship discusses both traditions when considering chronology and priority.
summary_zh: 约公元前七至六世纪，吕底亚王国首创官印打制琥珀金币，中国中原独立铸造青铜布币；硬币为贸易确立了标准化国家信用与交换尺度。
summary_en: Around the 7th–6th centuries BCE, Lydia pioneered officially stamped electrum coins, while China’s Central Plains independently cast bronze spade money, establishing state-backed standards for trade.
summary_ja: 紀元前7–6世紀頃、リディア王国が公的な刻印のあるエレクトラム貨を打ち出し、中国の中原では独立して青銅製の布銭が鋳造された。硬貨は、国家の信用に支えられた標準的な価値尺度を交易にもたらした。
